title: K-Means Clustering
subtitle: 3D Animated Point Cloud & Centroid Gliding
summary: Watch 40 points in 3D space connect via dashed lines to their nearest centroid, recolor, and pull centroids to new cluster centers.
intuition: Imagine dropping K colored magnets randomly into a 3D room filled with 40 floating metal marbles. First, each marble snaps to its closest magnet and takes on that magnet's color. Next, each magnet glides to the exact center of gravity of the marbles attached to it. Repeating those two steps causes the magnets to settle right in the middle of natural 3D neighborhoods!

howItWorks.title: Initialize K Centroids
howItWorks.detail: Place K starting centroids (glowing octahedrons) inside the 3D point cloud.

howItWorks.title: Compute 3D Euclidean Distances
howItWorks.detail: For every point xᵢ, measure the straight-line 3D distance to each centroid μ₁..μ_K (shown as dashed lines).

howItWorks.title: Assign Points (E-Step)
howItWorks.detail: Assign each point to its nearest centroid and recolor the point to match that cluster.

howItWorks.title: Glide Centroids to Cluster Means (M-Step)
howItWorks.detail: Recompute each centroid as the arithmetic mean (x̄, ȳ, z̄) of its assigned points and smoothly glide it there.

howItWorks.title: Check Convergence
howItWorks.detail: Stop when centroid movement Δμ_max drops below ε or Inertia (WCSS) stabilizes.

evaluationChart.title: Elbow Method (WCSS / Inertia vs. K)
evaluationChart.description: Identifies the optimal K at the elbow where marginal inertia reduction flattens.

advantages: Fast O(T · n · K · d) convergence that scales effortlessly to large datasets.
Easy geometric interpretation with explicit cluster centroid coordinates.
Works cleanly on compact, isotropic spherical clusters.
limitations: Must specify K upfront; poor initialization can converge to suboptimal local minima.
Struggles with non-convex crescent shapes or clusters of wildly different sizes.
Outliers pull cluster means away from the true dense core.
applications: Anchor box clustering in computer vision

formulas.description: Moves each centroid to the mean of its assigned points.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def kmeans_3d(X, k=3, iters=8):
    centroids = X[:k].copy()
    for step in range(iters):
        dists = np.linalg.norm(X[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :], axis=2)
        labels = np.argmin(dists, axis=1)
        centroids = np.array([X[labels == j].mean(axis=0) for j in range(k)])
    return centroids, labels
codeTemplates.production:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(40, 3)
km = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=42).fit(X)
print('Centroids:\n', km.cluster_centers_)
print('Inertia:', km.inertia_)
